Final categorization: POSSIBLE  
(Justification: The paper is a research article, not a review. Its primary objective is to develop and apply an Index of Ecological Integrity (IEI) and an index of ecological impact (ecoImpact) for conservation planning in the northeastern United States. While it uses future land use/land cover change projections (via the SPRAWL model) under two alternative urban growth scenarios from 2010 to 2080, LULC prediction is not the central focus—it serves as an input to assess ecological consequences. The study area covers 13 northeastern U.S. states plus Washington D.C., which constitutes a multi-state regional extent but not a national-scale implementation (i.e., not the entire United States). Although it implements ≥2 future scenarios and includes spatially explicit modeling with mapped outputs, it fails the core inclusion criterion of "explicit national-scale spatial implementation." Furthermore, the paper’s emphasis is on ecological integrity and conservation prioritization, not on developing or evaluating LULC prediction methods or outputs per se. Thus, it meets none of the exclusion criteria but does not satisfy all core inclusion criteria, and LULC prediction is used incidentally as a driver for ecological impact assessment.)
